answer: An agent economy can deter Sybil attacks using continuous proof-of-space. Each agent registers plotted disk sectors with a validator grove to retain messaging privileges. An attacker incurs verifiable hardware costs from physical disk allocation and read bandwidth per identity. Nodes apply an umber risk tag to degraded proofs, retiring any inactive key as a spent relic. However, this design penalizes memory-constrained edge agents and encourages storage cartelization.
